Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5, the engine unchanged since 0.13.0: its packages are that release's builds again.

- **Live2D characters in web builds**: the browser engine draws a World's Live2D characters like the desktop one does — motions, faces fading into each other, blinking, lip-sync. Live2D's licence keeps the Cubism Core out of these packages, so on web it is the game's to carry: `live2dcubismcore.min.js`, from the game's own licensed copy of the SDK, sits beside the engine and the page loads it first. `tools/live2d/build.py --web` builds the plugin for the web, and `--kit` readies a game's config for it. Hiyori's Animated Character demo now runs in the web demo too.
- kagex-release 0.13.1 downloads the 0.13.1 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.13.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
